- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days) are common; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak for next 5 days.
- Model often lags in early days of trend reversal; if sentiment shifts from negative to positive, forecast should rise faster than historical lag.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overpredicts mean price; apply downward bias of 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term volatility (e.g., alternating +0.33/-0.33), model tends to overfit noise; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average.
